stem: A child has watery diarrhoea and a calculated stool osmotic gap of 120 mOsm/kg; which clinical feature is most likely associated with this finding?

options.text: The diarrhoea stops when the child is nil by mouth
The diarrhoea continues unchanged during fasting
Stool microscopy shows leukocytes and red cells
The stool pH is neutral or slightly alkaline
The stool volume remains high overnight

explanation: Osmotic diarrhoea is the correct concept here. A stool osmotic gap greater than 100 mOsm/kg suggests osmotic diarrhoea, which improves or stops when the child fasts because the unabsorbed solute is no longer present in the gut.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because an osmotic stool osmotic gap greater than 100 mOsm/kg indicates osmotic diarrhoea, which typically stops when the child is fasting.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because diarrhoea that continues during fasting is more typical of secretory diarrhoea, which usually has a low stool osmotic gap.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because leukocytes and red cells suggest inflammatory diarrhoea or colitis, not osmotic diarrhoea.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because osmotic diarrhoea, especially from carbohydrate malabsorption, usually causes acidic stools from bacterial fermentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because persistent high overnight stool output is more suggestive of secretory diarrhoea than osmotic diarrhoea.

source.hint: Recall how the presence or absence of oral intake affects different types of watery diarrhea.
